# shopify_file (Resource)

A file in the store's media library: an image, a document, or an external video (YouTube, Vimeo). **A poor fit for Terraform in general:** files are content, uploaded and replaced in the admin and through product media all the time. Managing a few assets that are served from a URL, such as a logo or a download, fits; mirroring the whole library does not. Shopify fetches the file from `source`, which must be an `http://` or `https://` URL; uploads of local files, and with them new videos and 3D models, are not supported yet (roadmap). Videos and 3D models can still be imported or adopted. Destroying or replacing a file deletes it for good and breaks every product, page and theme that uses it, so that needs `allow_data_deletion = true` in state first. **Shopify also deletes a file when the last product that uses it lets go of it:** removing its ID from a `shopify_product`'s `media_ids` (guarded by that product's `allow_data_deletion`, not this one's), or destroying that product. The file's own `allow_data_deletion` can't prevent that; the next plan then shows a create for this resource. Removing this resource together with its ID in `media_ids`: if the file is destroyed before the product update, the product needs no flag; if the product update runs first, its guard fails the apply and nothing is deleted, so re-apply or set the product's flag. A file that already has the filename needs `adopt_existing = true`; destroy then leaves it in place. Import with the filename, or with the URL for an external video.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Shopify fetches the file from the URL. Local paths are not supported yet.
resource "shopify_file" "logo" {
  content_type = "IMAGE"
  filename     = "logo.png"
  source       = "https://assets.example.com/logo.png"
  # Fetch again when the file behind the URL changes.
  source_hash = "2026-10-27"
  alt         = "Company logo"

  # Deleting or replacing a file breaks everything that uses it; set this and apply before destroying.
  allow_data_deletion = false
}

resource "shopify_file" "datasheet" {
  content_type = "FILE"
  filename     = "datasheet.pdf"
  source       = "https://assets.example.com/datasheet.pdf"

  timeouts {
    create = "5m"
  }
}

# External videos have no filename; the URL is their key, in the form Shopify stores (youtu.be/<id> for YouTube).
resource "shopify_file" "howto" {
  content_type = "EXTERNAL_VIDEO"
  source       = "https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
}

# Take over a file that exists: without source, only alt is managed.
resource "shopify_file" "existing" {
  content_type   = "IMAGE"
  filename       = "hero.jpg"
  alt            = "Hero image"
  adopt_existing = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `content_type` (String) `IMAGE`, `FILE`, `VIDEO`, `EXTERNAL_VIDEO` or `MODEL_3D`. A file can't change its kind, so changing this replaces it.

### Optional

- `adopt_existing` (Boolean) Take over an existing file with the same natural key instead of failing. Destroy then only removes it from state. Defaults to `false`.
- `allow_data_deletion` (Boolean) Allow destroying or replacing this file, which deletes the data stored in it. Defaults to `false`. Must already be `true` in state when the delete runs, so set it in a separate apply first.
- `alt` (String) Alt text for screen readers. `""` clears it. Unset means unmanaged: the value set in the admin is kept.
- `filename` (String) The filename with its extension, unique per shop and the import key. Required for every content type except `EXTERNAL_VIDEO`, where it must be unset. ASCII letters, digits, `.`, `_` and `-` only, because Shopify rewrites anything else. Changing it renames the file in place and **changes its CDN URL**, so links in pages and themes break; images and generic files only. A different extension replaces the file, and it must match the extension of the `source` URL (Shopify refuses the file otherwise, which is checked at plan time).
- `source` (String) The `http://` or `https://` URL Shopify fetches the file from; for `EXTERNAL_VIDEO`, the video URL, which is read back. Shopify rewrites video URLs (`https://youtu.be/<id>` for YouTube), and the duplicate check, adoption and import only match that form, so use it. Required to create a file; without it only `adopt_existing` works. Not readable for hosted files: Read keeps the configured value, and an imported file has none (unmanaged). A new value replaces the content in place for `IMAGE` and `FILE`; for the other content types it replaces the file. Not allowed for `VIDEO` and `MODEL_3D` yet (roadmap).
- `source_hash` (String) Not interpreted; any change fetches `source` again, like a change of `source` itself. A file behind a URL that changes later is otherwise invisible to Terraform, because the URL is not fetched at plan time.
- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) File GID. Its kind follows the content type (`MediaImage`, `GenericFile`, `Video`, `ExternalVideo`, `Model3d`); a product's `media_ids` take it as is, except `GenericFile` (`content_type = "FILE"`), which can't be product media.
- `url` (String) The public URL of the file; for an external video, the video URL. Changes with the filename and with a content update (`?v=`).

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the create, as a duration such as `30s` or `10m`.
- `update` (String) How long to wait for the update, as a duration such as `30s` or `10m`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# <filename>, or the video URL in the form Shopify stores for an external video
terraform import shopify_file.logo logo.png
terraform import shopify_file.howto "https://youtu.be/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
```
